statement: A pancake recipe uses 3 cups of milk, and one cup holds 250 ml. Leo makes the recipe 3 times. Milk is sold in 1-litre cartons. How many cartons must he buy?

choices.misconception: I worked out the milk for just one recipe, 750 ml, which fits in one carton.
I found he needs 2250 ml, which is 2 and a quarter litres, and rounded down to 2.
I counted the cups of milk, 3 times 3, instead of the cartons.
I thought 1 litre is 100 ml, so 2250 ml needed 22 and a half cartons, which I rounded to 23.

hints: How many cups does he use in all?
Find the total milk in millilitres, change it to litres, and remember he cannot buy part of a carton.
He uses $3 \times 3 = 9$ cups, which is $9 \times 250 = 2250$ ml.

solutions.reliable: Three recipes use $3 \times 3 = 9$ cups. Nine cups hold $9 \times 250 = 2250$ ml. One litre is 1000 ml, so 2 cartons give only 2000 ml, which is not enough. He must buy 3 cartons. The transferable idea: when you can only buy whole packs, round up, not to the nearest.
solutions.elegant: Four cups of 250 ml make exactly 1 litre. Nine cups is two full litres and one more cup, so he needs a third carton.

whyOnTest: Converting millilitres to litres and then rounding up to whole cartons is a two-step trap common in Kangaroo word problems.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
